High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Govt. Civil Sectt. Lko And 3 Othe

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The accused-applicants seek bail in Case Crime No.130 of 2023 under sections 323, 376-D, 504 IPC and 5G/6 of POCSO Act, P.S. Sandi, District Hardoi.

3. The first information report was initially lodged under sections 354, 504 IPC by the victim herself stating that on 10.03.2023 at about 9.00 pm, Monu and Kuldeep (applicants) as well as Rakesh,
Abhishek and Pintu started hitting the victim and Monu caught hold her hand.
She also stated in the first information report that the acts were done with an intention to outrage her modesty.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Her statement was also recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C.
In the said statement, the victim stated that Monu and Kuldeep starting misbehaving the victim and started hitting her.
She also stated that Pintu and Kuldeep have committed the offence under section 376 IPC.

Subsequently, the victim was subjected to medical examination on 11.03.2023, which is on record, which shows contused swelling on the upper side of the left shoulder and there was a complaint of pain in the abdomen and no visible injuries were shown over the body in question.

4. In the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C., which was recorded on 15.03.2023 after about five days, the victim levelled allegations of the commission of the offence under section 376 IPC against all the four accused persons.
The medical examination of the victim, after the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C., was done on 22.03.2023 which does not disclose any injury on any part of the body.
The age of the victim, as per the high school certificate and medical, is seventeen years.
5. The counsel for the applicant argues that the first information report was initially lodged under sections 354 and 504 IPC.
Subsequently, in the statement under section 161 Cr.P.C., only two persons were named and the medical report dated 11.03.2023 does not corroborate the happening of offence under section 376 IPC.

Subsequently, in the statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
on 15.03.2023, the victim made allegations of the offence under section 376 Cr.P.C. against four persons.

He argues that the statement also records that there was ongoing dispute between the parties and thus, on the basis of it, the allegation levelled in the statement under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. are incorrect and has been made only to falsely implicate the applicants with the offence in question.
The applicants are in custody since 29.03.2023 ans they have no criminal antecedents.
6. No one appears for the complainant despite notice by the AGA.
Learned AGA opposes the bail application by arguing that the statement under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. clearly implicate the applicants with the offence in question.
He argues that based upon the High School certificate, the age of the victim is 17 years and thus, the bail application deserves to be rejected.

7. Considering the submissions made at the bar, prima-facie, there is huge variance in the allegations levelled in the first information report and in the statement under section 161 Cr.P.C and subsequently in the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C.

No allegation of the commission of the offence under section 376 IPC was made in the first information report and the medical of the victim does not support her statement under section 161 and the second medical done after recording of the statement under section 164Cr.P.C. also does not corroborate the statement.

Thus, looking to the huge inconsistencies in the statements coupled with the fact that the applicants have no criminal antecedents and are in custody since 29.03.2023, the applicants are entitled for the bail, as such, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicants Monu Alias Ramnaresh and Kuldeep be released on bail in aforesaid first information report number subject to their furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicants shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
